questions.stem: Which phase of the cell cycle is known as the period of preparation for cell division?
questions.solution: Interphase is the phase where the cell grows and prepares for division by replicating its DNA and organelles. Mitosis is the actual process of cell division, meiosis is a specialized type of division for gametes, and cytokinesis is the final stage where the cell splits into two. Interphase is the correct answer because it involves the preparation necessary for division.

questions.stem: Which phase of the cell cycle is described as the phase between two successive M phases?
questions.solution: Interphase is the phase during which the cell grows and prepares for division, occurring between two successive M phases. The M phase involves actual cell division, while prophase and telophase are stages within the M phase, not the period between them. Therefore, interphase is the correct answer.

questions.stem: What is the main difference between mitosis and meiosis?
choices: Mitosis produces four daughter cells, meiosis produces two
Mitosis involves one division, meiosis involves two
Mitosis is the reduction division, meiosis is the equational division
Mitosis occurs only in plant cells, meiosis occurs only in animal cells
questions.solution: Mitosis involves one division, while meiosis involves two, which results in a reduction of chromosome number. The other options are incorrect because mitosis produces two daughter cells, not four, and both processes occur in plant and animal cells. Meiosis is the reduction division, while mitosis is the equational division.

questions.stem: What is the result of crossing over during meiosis?
questions.solution: Crossing over during meiosis leads to an increase in genetic variability. It is an enzyme-mediated process where genetic material is exchanged between homologous chromosomes. This results in new combinations of genes, which is essential for evolution. The other options describe different aspects of meiosis, not the result of crossing over.

hi.stem: मेयोसिस के दौरान क्रॉसिंग ओवर का परिणाम क्या होता है?
hi.solution: मेयोसिस के दौरान क्रॉसिंग ओवर आनुवंशिक विविधता में वृद्धि के कारण होता है। यह एक एंजाइम-माध्यमित प्रक्रिया है जहां जैविक सामग्री का एक होमोलॉग क्रोमोसोम के बीच आदान-प्रदान होता है। इससे नए जीन के संयोजन बनते हैं, जो विकास के लिए आवश्यक है। अन्य विकल्प मेयोसिस के अलग-अलग पहलू बताते हैं, क्रॉसिंग ओवर के परिणाम नहीं।
hi.critique: The translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses appropriate biological terminology in Hindi.

mr.stem: मेयोसिस दरम्यान क्रॉसिंग ओव्हरचा परिणाम काय असतो?
mr.solution: मेयोसिस दरम्यान क्रॉसिंग ओव्हरमुळे जेनेटिक विविधतेत वाढ होते. हे एन्झाइम-मार्गदर्शित प्रक्रिया असून होमोलॉगस क्रोमोझोममध्ये जीनिटिक विषय बदलला जातो. हे नवीन जीनच्या संयोजनामुळे होते, जे विकासासाठी आवश्यक आहे. इतर विकल्प मेयोसिसच्या वेगळ्या बाजूंना दर्शवतात, क्रॉसिंग ओव्हरच्या परिणामांना नाही.

questions.stem: If a cell has 46 chromosomes in its nucleus, how many chromosomes will each daughter cell have after mitosis?
questions.solution: Mitosis is a process where a single cell divides into two identical daughter cells. Since the original cell has 46 chromosomes, each daughter cell will also have 46 chromosomes because the genetic material is equally distributed. 23 would be the result of meiosis, and 92 and 184 are not possible because mitosis does not double the chromosome count.

questions.stem: Which phase of meiosis is characterised by the pairing of homologous chromosomes?
questions.solution: Prophase I is the phase where homologous chromosomes pair up in a process called synapsis. The other phases do not involve this pairing. Metaphase I involves alignment, Anaphase I involves separation, and Telophase I involves the formation of two daughter cells.

questions.stem: In which of the following tissues would mitotic cell division most likely occur in a human body?
questions.solution: Bone marrow contains stem cells that continuously divide to produce new blood cells, making it a site of frequent mitotic division.
